synopsis: 3DGS provides a log-trained scene representation as an alternative to explicit geometry conversion; neural reconstruction requires multi-camera logs with accurate poses, optional lidar and GPU compute [f3992, f4226]. Chapter 7 positions neural re-simulation as approximately closed-loop near the recorded trajectory, but limited for large viewpoint shifts and new sensor mounting positions, with very low off-road maturity and on-road-only evidence [f5722, f5723, f5725]. Quantitative results reinforce that limitation: XLD’s June 2024 preprint, with a 2025 v3 using synthetic CARLA data, reported PSNR falling from 30.87 dB at zero lateral shift to 19.17 dB at 4 m, while the August 2026 MV² preprint reported drone-trained 3DGS falling from 29.13 to 10.36 dB when switching to car viewpoints [f4001, f4008]. Industry preference for 3DGS editability therefore does not establish superior viewpoint robustness: XLD found two NeRF-based methods held up better than its 3DGS variant at 4 m offsets [f4329]. ISPRS 2024 reported Unreal Engine 5 performance of 60 FPS for a single building and 17 FPS for a 23-million-Gaussian terrain scene, providing hardware-in-the-loop-relevant performance results rather than resolving the generalisation gap [f3893, f3894, f4010].

relations.note: Log-trained scene representations enable re-rendering recorded scenes for neural re-simulation.
